name: Lou Khan
life: “I worked breakfast on the day our street lost power until noon.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Tideline Market, where Lou picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: She ordered two slices after her husband died. I wrapped the other half for whoever sat at his table.
appearance: Lou is easy to recognize by a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a boxy denim jacket with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Lou folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
personality: Lou enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To keep one lunchtime place open for an unaccompanied diner.
family: Grey Ibrahim is Lou’s cousin raised in the same household. Lou brings a spare shopping bag. Grey chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Rent in a biscuit tin*, Grey says, “I used her kitchen as my savings bank when I sold pills.”
connections: Blake Baker. A new deli owner learns who used to eat the other half.
